what it says: *** Santiago Apostol y San Nicolas (la Iglesia Matriz de Mendoza), Baptism Records 1899-1901 ***; DGS film 004597291, image 69, ark 3:1:939X-HF9M-7S, *** waypoint Q633-3DR ***. Baptism of *** 6 January 1900 *** by the cura Dr. J. Juan Jordan. *** PLATE READ 9 October 2026 - there is no AI transcript for this image. ***
what it settles: *** MARIA ADELA, hija legitima de D. CARLOS LERENA y ADELA CARNIGLIA *** - a daughter this archive did not hold. *** THE CLERK GIVES NO MONTH FOR THE BIRTH: *** 'nacio el quince del ano pasado', so the fifteenth of some month in 1899, and the formula is left incomplete rather than finished for him.

what it says: The parents are '*** orien[tales], domiciliados en este Curato ***' - the word runs over the line end and is read across both halves at full magnification
what it settles: *** CARLOS LERENA IS ORIENTAL - URUGUAYAN. *** data/cajon-985-origins.tsv had him as 'Not established'. *** THAT MAKES FOUR OF THE DRAWER'S TRACEABLE FATHERS, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM URUGUAYAN OR MARRIED IN URUGUAY *** - Gilberto, Alejandro Maximo, Nemesio Ramon and now Carlos. *** IT STRENGTHENS A BASE RATE RATHER THAN MAKING A LINK: *** in this generation an Argentine Lerena is a Uruguayan family's son far more often than not, and *** JUAN CARLOS LERENA, WHO LEFT NO TRACE AT ROSARIO AT ALL, FITS THAT SHAPE. ***

what it says: 'fueron padrinos *** Domingo Simois POR ABELINO LERENA *** y Lucia L. de Simois' - the act names a proxy and the man he stood for, and both signed: *** Dgo. Simois *** and *** Lucia Lemos de Simois ***
what it settles: *** AN AVELINO LERENA IS GODFATHER TO CARLOS'S DAUGHTER, BY PROXY, AT MENDOZA IN 1900. *** data/cajon-985-origins.tsv noted that Carlos named a son *** AVELINO CARLOS *** in 1904 and called it 'suggestive only'. *** IT IS NO LONGER ONLY A FORENAME: there is a real Avelino Lerena in his circle. *** *** AND IT IS STILL NOT AN IDENTIFICATION. *** This register holds *** FOUR *** men of that name - Avelino Lerena Fernandez (b.1815, head of the Lerena Traibel branch), Avelino Eduardo Lerena Traibel, Avelino Pedro Joaquin Silvestre and Avelino Lerena Villademoros - and the act gives no patronymic, no age and no residence for him.

what was read: *** WHY THE CAUTION IS NOT BOILERPLATE HERE ***
what it says: The adjacent row of data/cajon-985-origins.tsv, for *** ARTURO LERENA ***, was written as 'Montevideo 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel' and *** WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY *** as a conflation with *** JUAN ARTURO LERENA TRAIBEL ***, whose wife was Ema Regules
what it settles: *** THIS ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY ATTACHED A CAJON 985 FATHER TO AVELINO LERENA ONCE AND BEEN WRONG. *** *** SO CARLOS IS RECORDED AS ORIENTAL, WITH AN AVELINO IN HIS CIRCLE, AND NOT PLACED IN ANY BRANCH. *** *** WHAT WOULD PLACE HIM: *** his own marriage to Adela Carniglia, which would name his parents; or the second daughter's act.

what was read: *** AND A SECOND DAUGHTER, NOT YET OPENED ***
what it says: The same parent-pair query returns a third child: *** MARIA MERCEDES LERENA ***, Argentina, Mendoza, Catholic Church Records 1665-1975, ark 3:1:1:QVN9-3S53 (index)
what it settles: *** THREE CHILDREN NOW WHERE THE DRAWER SHOWED ONE: *** Avelino Carlos (1904), Maria Adela (b.1899, bap. 1900) and Maria Mercedes. *** HER ACT IS UNREAD *** and is the cheapest next step on this man, because a second baptism may give what this one does not - his own parents, or a place he was natural of.

what was read: *** AND A SPELLING THIS REGISTER HAS CARRIED WRONG ***
what it says: The act writes the mother *** ADELA CARNIGLIA ***, with an r; the FamilySearch index of the army card agrees
what it settles: *** THIS REGISTER HAS HELD HER AS 'ADELA CAMIGLIA' SINCE 13 SEPTEMBER ***, without the r, and so has her husband's row. *** THE ACT IS THE BETTER WITNESS AND THE INDEX AGREES WITH IT ***, so CARNIGLIA is recorded as the reading and CAMIGLIA kept beside it as what this archive used to say. *** CARNIGLIA IS AN ITALIAN SURNAME *** - she may be Uruguayan-born of Italian parents, which is what 'orientales' in the plural would cover.
